definitions.explanation: The physical effect of electric current passing through the body. Composed of 感 (feel/sense) + 電 (electricity). Used as a noun or suru-verb. Ranges from a minor jolt to a fatal shock.

examples.japanese: {濡|ぬ}れた{手|て}でコンセントに{触|さわ}ると{感電|かんでん}する。
examples.english: You'll get an electric shock if you touch an outlet with wet hands.

examples.japanese: {工事|こうじ}{現場|げんば}で{感電|かんでん}{事故|じこ}が{起|お}きた。
examples.english: An electrocution accident occurred at the construction site.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{家電|かでん}は{感電|かんでん}の{危険|きけん}があるので、{定期的|ていきてき}に{点検|てんけん}したほうがいい。
examples.english: Old appliances can be a shock hazard, so it's a good idea to inspect them regularly.

notes:
USAGE:
{感電|かんでん} can be used as a noun ({感電|かんでん}{事故|じこ} — electrocution accident) or as a suru-verb ({感電|かんでん}する — to get shocked). It covers the full range from a mild static shock to a dangerous or fatal electrocution.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {感電|かんでん}する (get an electric shock)
- {感電|かんでん}{事故|じこ} (electrocution accident)
- {感電|かんでん}{死|し} (death by electrocution)
- {感電|かんでん}の{危険|きけん} (risk of electric shock)
- {感電|かんでん}{防止|ぼうし} (shock prevention)
